answer: The vertex is the register where identities are anchored and keyed, so a clone reusing a key collides with the identity already seated. A mirror is one forged identity. Anchoring burns ember for good, priced at the count of identities already anchored across every vertex, so splitting the fleet buys nothing: the thousandth mirror costs a thousand ember, and a thousand clones cost half a million. Ember comes only from clients paying for judged work. It breaks if ember is minted on demand or audits never land.
